To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the partition function of a class S theory on a torus is a $\tau$-functional of the isomonodrome problem of the corresponding Seiberg-Wittn integrable system.

the isomonodrome deformation problem of a flat connection on a punctured torus can be mapped to $W_N$, the partition function of a class S gauge theory, and that the $\tau$-functions of the corresponding Seiberg-Witgen integrable systems are proportional to the dual partition functions.

the partition function of a class of 4D N=2 supersymmetric theories, which we call "circular quiver" theories, can be expressed in terms of a tau-function of an integrable system, the isomonodronic deformation problem, and that this tau-function can be computed in terms of $W_N$ fermions on a torus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of class S theories of type A and D on punctured torus and the relation to isomonodromy problems.
two different aspects of the theory of class S theories.
the study of the relation between class $S$ theories of type A and isomonodric deformations of flat connections on the torus with puncture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the $\tau$ function of the isomonodronic deformation problem is proportional to the partition function of the dual class S gauge theory, the proportionality constant being a non trivial solution of the Seibert-Witten integrable hierarchy.

class S theories on the torus can be obtained by isomonodromy deformations of flat connections on the torus and that these deformations correspond to the free fermion correlator of the dual gauge theory.
the isomonodronic deformations of the flat SL(N) connection are related to the $W_N$ conformal blocks of the dual gauge theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the $\tau$-functions for isomonodromy problems on punctured torus can be expressed as correlators of fermions on the punctured torus.
we show how to obtain the dual gauge theory on the torus by deautonomizing the Seiberg–Witten integrable system and by computing the $W_N$ fermions on the punctured torus.

the $\tau$-functions for isomonodromy deformations of the flat SL(N) connection on the torus with N-1 punctures are proportional to the Nekrasov partition functions of a class S theory with N-1 flavor punctures on the torus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the partition function for class S theories on the torus is a $\tau$- function for an isomonodromy problem on the two dimensional sphere, which is a generalization of the Seifert problem.
the $\tau$-functions of the deautonomous Seiberg-Witzen integrable systems are in fact partition functions for class S theories on a torus with puncture and are thus non trivial functions.
the $\Omega$-deformed partition function of a 3d gauge theory can be expressed in terms of $W_N$ fermion correlators.
